I never believed there was anything sacred about her. It was more like a lingering perfume she had left—a scent of musk and amber rather than the fragrance of holiness. I was just beginning to choke on the fumes of hothouse flowers and sprinkled essences when I thought to open the window and step out onto the balcony. It was moonlit and gaslit besides, and very still and calm. The balcony had a chair or two; I sat down and took out a cigar—I will take one now, if you'll excuse me."
